namespace sys.crypto.ed25519_error

public enum Kind {
    InvalidLength
    NonCanonical
    InvalidPoint
    InvalidScalar
}

namespace sys.crypto.sha256

powerOfTwo exponent: Int -> UInt64 {
    UInt64(1) => power!
    0 => powerIndex!
    powerIndex! < exponent -> while {
        power! * 2 => power!
        powerIndex! + 1 => powerIndex!
    }
    power!
}

rotateRight word: UInt64, count: Int -> UInt64 {
    count -> powerOfTwo => lowDivisor
    (32 - count) -> powerOfTwo => highMultiplier
    word / lowDivisor + (word % lowDivisor) * highMultiplier
}

xor3 xorLeft: UInt64, xorMiddle: UInt64, xorRight: UInt64 -> UInt64 {
    UInt64(0) => result!
    UInt64(1) => place!
    xorLeft => left!
    xorMiddle => middle!
    xorRight => right!
    0 => bit!
    bit! < 32 -> while {
        ((left! % 2) + (middle! % 2) + (right! % 2)) % 2 => parity
        result! + parity * place! => result!
        left! / 2 => left!
        middle! / 2 => middle!
        right! / 2 => right!
        place! * 2 => place!
        bit! + 1 => bit!
    }
    result!
}

choose selector: UInt64, whenSet: UInt64, whenClear: UInt64 -> UInt64 {
    UInt64(0) => result!
    UInt64(1) => place!
    selector => selectBits!
    whenSet => setBits!
    whenClear => clearBits!
    0 => bit!
    bit! < 32 -> while {
        selectBits! % 2 => selected
        selected == 1 -> if { setBits! % 2 } else { clearBits! % 2 } => chosenBit
        result! + chosenBit * place! => result!
        selectBits! / 2 => selectBits!
        setBits! / 2 => setBits!
        clearBits! / 2 => clearBits!
        place! * 2 => place!
        bit! + 1 => bit!
    }
    result!
}

majority first: UInt64, second: UInt64, third: UInt64 -> UInt64 {
    UInt64(0) => result!
    UInt64(1) => place!
    first => left!
    second => middle!
    third => right!
    0 => bit!
    bit! < 32 -> while {
        (left! % 2) + (middle! % 2) + (right! % 2) => count
        count >= 2 -> if { result! + place! => result! }
        left! / 2 => left!
        middle! / 2 => middle!
        right! / 2 => right!
        place! * 2 => place!
        bit! + 1 => bit!
    }
    result!
}

largeSigma0 value: UInt64 -> UInt64 {
    value -> rotateRight(2) => first
    value -> rotateRight(13) => second
    value -> rotateRight(22) => third
    xor3(first, second, third)
}

largeSigma1 value: UInt64 -> UInt64 {
    value -> rotateRight(6) => first
    value -> rotateRight(11) => second
    value -> rotateRight(25) => third
    xor3(first, second, third)
}

smallSigma0 value: UInt64 -> UInt64 {
    value -> rotateRight(7) => first
    value -> rotateRight(18) => second
    value / 8 => third
    xor3(first, second, third)
}

smallSigma1 value: UInt64 -> UInt64 {
    value -> rotateRight(17) => first
    value -> rotateRight(19) => second
    value / 1_024 => third
    xor3(first, second, third)
}

roundConstants: -> [UInt64] => [
    1_116_352_408, 1_899_447_441, 3_049_323_471, 3_921_009_573,
    961_987_163, 1_508_970_993, 2_453_635_748, 2_870_763_221,
    3_624_381_080, 310_598_401, 607_225_278, 1_426_881_987,
    1_925_078_388, 2_162_078_206, 2_614_888_103, 3_248_222_580,
    3_835_390_401, 4_022_224_774, 264_347_078, 604_807_628,
    770_255_983, 1_249_150_122, 1_555_081_692, 1_996_064_986,
    2_554_220_882, 2_821_834_349, 2_952_996_808, 3_210_313_671,
    3_336_571_891, 3_584_528_711, 113_926_993, 338_241_895,
    666_307_205, 773_529_912, 1_294_757_372, 1_396_182_291,
    1_695_183_700, 1_986_661_051, 2_177_026_350, 2_456_956_037,
    2_730_485_921, 2_820_302_411, 3_259_730_800, 3_345_764_771,
    3_516_065_817, 3_600_352_804, 4_094_571_909, 275_423_344,
    430_227_734, 506_948_616, 659_060_556, 883_997_877,
    958_139_571, 1_322_822_218, 1_537_002_063, 1_747_873_779,
    1_955_562_222, 2_024_104_815, 2_227_730_452, 2_361_852_424,
    2_428_436_474, 2_756_734_187, 3_204_031_479, 3_329_325_298]

public digest source: [UInt8] -> [UInt8; 32] {
    roundConstants() => constants
    [UInt64(1_779_033_703), 3_144_134_277, 1_013_904_242, 2_773_480_762,
        1_359_893_119, 2_600_822_924, 528_734_635, 1_541_459_225] => hash!
    UInt64(source -> len) * 8 => bitLength
    UIntSize(source -> len) + 1 => paddedWithoutLength
    ((paddedWithoutLength + 8 + 63) / 64) * 64 => paddedLength
    UIntSize(0) => blockStart!
    blockStart! < paddedLength -> while {
        [UInt64(0); 64] => words!
        0 => wordIndex!
        wordIndex! < 16 -> while {
            UInt64(0) => word!
            0 => byteIndex!
            byteIndex! < 4 -> while {
                blockStart! + UIntSize(wordIndex! * 4 + byteIndex!) => sourceIndex
                UInt64(0) => byteValue!
                sourceIndex < UIntSize(source -> len) -> if {
                    UInt64(source[Int(sourceIndex)]) => byteValue!
                } else {
                    sourceIndex == UIntSize(source -> len) -> if {
                        128 => byteValue!
                    } else {
                        sourceIndex >= paddedLength - 8 -> if {
                            Int(paddedLength - 1 - sourceIndex) * 8 => shift
                            (bitLength / (shift -> powerOfTwo)) % 256 => byteValue!
                        }
                    }
                }
                word! * 256 + byteValue! => word!
                byteIndex! + 1 => byteIndex!
            }
            word! => words![wordIndex!]
            wordIndex! + 1 => wordIndex!
        }
        16 => scheduleIndex!
        scheduleIndex! < 64 -> while {
            words![scheduleIndex! - 2] -> smallSigma1 => sigma1
            words![scheduleIndex! - 15] -> smallSigma0 => sigma0
            sigma1 + words![scheduleIndex! - 7] + sigma0 + words![scheduleIndex! - 16] => sum
            sum % 4_294_967_296 => words![scheduleIndex!]
            scheduleIndex! + 1 => scheduleIndex!
        }
        hash![0] => a!
        hash![1] => b!
        hash![2] => c!
        hash![3] => d!
        hash![4] => e!
        hash![5] => f!
        hash![6] => g!
        hash![7] => h!
        0 => round!
        round! < 64 -> while {
            e! -> largeSigma1 => sigma1
            choose(e!, f!, g!) => selected
            (h! + sigma1 + selected + constants[round!] + words![round!]) % 4_294_967_296 => temporary1
            a! -> largeSigma0 => sigma0
            majority(a!, b!, c!) => common
            (sigma0 + common) % 4_294_967_296 => temporary2
            g! => h!
            f! => g!
            e! => f!
            (d! + temporary1) % 4_294_967_296 => e!
            c! => d!
            b! => c!
            a! => b!
            (temporary1 + temporary2) % 4_294_967_296 => a!
            round! + 1 => round!
        }
        (hash![0] + a!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![0]
        (hash![1] + b!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![1]
        (hash![2] + c!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![2]
        (hash![3] + d!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![3]
        (hash![4] + e!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![4]
        (hash![5] + f!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![5]
        (hash![6] + g!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![6]
        (hash![7] + h!) % 4_294_967_296 => hash![7]
        blockStart! + 64 => blockStart!
    }
    [UInt8(0); 32] => output!
    0 => outputIndex!
    0 => hashIndex!
    hashIndex! < 8 -> while {
        3 => byteIndex!
        byteIndex! >= 0 -> while {
            UInt8(hash![hashIndex!] / ((byteIndex! * 8) -> powerOfTwo) % 256) => byte
            byte => output![outputIndex!]
            outputIndex! + 1 => outputIndex!
            byteIndex! - 1 => byteIndex!
        }
        hashIndex! + 1 => hashIndex!
    }
    output!
}

namespace sys.crypto.x25519

import sys.crypto.field25519 as field
import sys.crypto.random as random

scalarBit scalar: [UInt8], bitIndex: Int -> UInt64 {
    bitIndex % 8 => withinByte
    1 => divisor!
    0 => index!
    index! < withinByte -> while {
        divisor! * 2 => divisor!
        index! + 1 => index!
    }
    UInt64(scalar[bitIndex / 8]) / UInt64(divisor!) % 2
}

swapIf swap: UInt64, left: mut [UInt64; 16], right: mut [UInt64; 16] -> Unit {
    1 - swap => keep
    0 => index!
    index! < 16 -> while {
        left[index!] => leftValue
        right[index!] => rightValue
        leftValue * keep + rightValue * swap => left[index!]
        rightValue * keep + leftValue * swap => right[index!]
        index! + 1 => index!
    }
}

public scalarMultiply privateScalar: [UInt8], coordinate: [UInt8] -> [UInt8; 32] {
    field.byteZeros() => scalar!
    0 => scalarIndex!
    scalarIndex! < 32 -> while {
        privateScalar[scalarIndex!] => scalar![scalarIndex!]
        scalarIndex! + 1 => scalarIndex!
    }
    scalar![0] - scalar![0] % 8 => scalar![0]
    scalar![31] % 64 + 64 => scalar![31]

    coordinate -> field.decode => x1
    field.one() => x2!
    field.zeros() => z2!
    coordinate -> field.decode => x3!
    field.one() => z3!
    UInt64(0) => swap!
    254 => bitIndex!
    bitIndex! >= 0 -> while {
        scalarBit(scalar!, bitIndex!) => scalarValue
        (swap! + scalarValue) % 2 => shouldSwap
        swapIf(shouldSwap, x2!, x3!)
        swapIf(shouldSwap, z2!, z3!)
        scalarValue => swap!

        field.add(x2!, z2!) => a
        field.square(a) => aa
        field.subtract(x2!, z2!) => b
        field.square(b) => bb
        field.subtract(aa, bb) => e
        field.add(x3!, z3!) => c
        field.subtract(x3!, z3!) => d
        field.multiply(d, a) => da
        field.multiply(c, b) => cb
        field.add(da, cb) -> field.square => nextX3
        field.subtract(da, cb) -> field.square -> field.multiply(x1) => nextZ3
        field.multiply(aa, bb) => nextX2
        e -> field.multiplySmall(121_665) -> field.add(aa) -> field.multiply(e) => nextZ2
        x3! -> field.replace(nextX3)
        z3! -> field.replace(nextZ3)
        x2! -> field.replace(nextX2)
        z2! -> field.replace(nextZ2)
        bitIndex! - 1 => bitIndex!
    }
    swapIf(swap!, x2!, x3!)
    swapIf(swap!, z2!, z3!)
    z2! -> field.invert -> field.multiply(x2!) -> field.encode
}

public publicKey privateScalar: [UInt8] -> [UInt8; 32] {
    field.byteZeros() => basePoint!
    9 => basePoint![0]
    scalarMultiply(privateScalar, basePoint!)
}

# Generates an independently owned scalar from the operating system
# cryptographic random source. scalarMultiply applies the RFC 7748 clamp at
# use time, so the stored private bytes retain their full random input.
public generatePrivateKey: -> Result<[UInt8; 32], random.Error> uses Random {
    32 -> random.bytes -> when {
        Ok(bytes) {
            field.byteZeros() => privateKey!
            0 => index!
            index! < 32 -> while {
                bytes[index!] => privateKey![index!]
                index! + 1 => index!
            }
            Result<[UInt8; 32], random.Error>.Ok(privateKey!)
        }
        Err(error) { Result<[UInt8; 32], random.Error>.Err(error) }
    }
}

namespace sys.event

public struct MouseEvent {
    x: Int
    y: Int
    delta: Int
    button: Int
    kind: MouseEventKind
}

# Mouse event kinds are stable across platform adapters.
public enum MouseEventKind {
    Move
    ButtonDown
    ButtonUp
    Wheel
}

# Defines what a hot producer does when its fixed-capacity queue is full.
public enum EventOverflowPolicy {
    DropNewest
    DropOldest
    CoalesceMotion
}

# Creates a hot, affine mouse event source. capacity is fixed for the source
# lifetime. CoalesceMotion replaces the newest pending move and prioritizes
# button and wheel transitions without growing the queue.
public mouseEvents capacity: Int, overflow: EventOverflowPolicy -> EventStream<MouseEvent> uses Console = intrinsic

namespace sys.file

import sys.runtime as rt
import sys.path as path

# File is an affine native resource. Its private token cannot be constructed or
# copied by user code, and leaving the owner scope closes it deterministically.
public struct File {
    token: UInt64
}

# FileWriter is a separate affine capability, so read-only and write-only
# handles cannot be mixed accidentally. openWrite creates or truncates a file.
# Its syncAsync flow member is a durable-data barrier, not a user-buffer flush.
public struct FileWriter {
    token: UInt64
}

public struct AtomicReplaceRequest {
    temporary: Text
    destination: Text
}

# SourceText is an affine compiler input. A borrowed literal has no mapping;
# a mapped file owns its mapping until the SourceText owner is dropped.
public struct SourceText {
    token: UInt64
}

# User-defined values opt into binary serialization by constructing their own
# canonical byte representation. This deliberately avoids writing a struct's
# target-dependent in-memory ABI layout.
public trait BinarySerializable {
    serialize: self -> [UInt8; ~]
}

borrowText text: Text -> SourceText = intrinsic

public borrowBytes bytes: ref [UInt8; ~] -> SourceText = intrinsic

mapText path: Text -> SourceText uses File = intrinsic

# Maps an owned target-explicit Path without manufacturing a Text view whose
# lifetime could outlive the Path storage.
public mapPath value: path.Path -> SourceText uses File = intrinsic

public openRead path: Text -> Result<File, Text> uses File = intrinsic

public openReadAsync path: Text -> async Result<File, Text> uses File = intrinsic

# Reads standard input to EOF into an affine compiler-input buffer. The owner
# releases the buffer deterministically at scope exit.
public readStandardInput: -> SourceText uses File = intrinsic

# Reads at most `capacity` bytes from standard input in one blocking operation.
# A zero-length result is EOF. The returned SourceText owns its heap buffer.
public readStandardInputChunk capacity: UIntSize -> SourceText uses File = intrinsic

public openWrite path: Text -> Result<FileWriter, Text> uses File = intrinsic

public openWriteAsync path: Text -> async Result<FileWriter, Text> uses File = intrinsic

# Synchronous compiler/cache durability primitives. The affine writer closes
# deterministically at scope exit before atomicReplace publishes its temp file.
public sync writer: FileWriter -> Bool uses File = intrinsic

public atomicReplace request: AtomicReplaceRequest -> Bool uses File = intrinsic

openIntWriter path: Text -> Unit uses File {
    path -> rt.openIntWriter
}

writeInt value: Int -> Unit uses File {
    value -> rt.writeInt
}

closeIntWriter: -> Unit uses File {
    rt.closeIntWriter()
}

openIntReader path: Text -> Unit uses File {
    path -> rt.openIntReader
}

closestInt target: Int -> Int uses File {
    target -> rt.closestInt
}

closeIntReader: -> Unit uses File {
    rt.closeIntReader()
}

# Generic canonical binary writer. Existing Int-specific names remain for the
# sorted Int64 demo format.
openWriter path: Text -> Unit uses File = intrinsic

write<T> value: T -> Unit uses File = intrinsic

closeWriter: -> Unit uses File = intrinsic

# Generic canonical binary reader. Ok(None) is clean EOF; partial scalars,
# invalid Bool/CodePoint encodings, and operating-system failures return
# "truncated", "invalid", and "io" errors.
openReader path: Text -> Unit uses File = intrinsic

read<T>: -> Result<Option<T>, Text> uses File = intrinsic

# Asynchronous scalar reads use the shared native file worker. The operation
# returns an affine Task and therefore composes with the ordinary await and
# cancellation rules without exposing callbacks or executor handles.
readAsync<T>: -> async Result<Option<T>, Text> uses File = intrinsic

closeReader: -> Unit uses File = intrinsic

namespace sys.process

# Runs one executable directly and connects only its standard output to a
# newly created or truncated file. Arguments remain literal argv entries; no
# shell parsing or command-string quoting is introduced.
public struct RunToFileRequest {
    argv: [Text; ~]
    output: Text
}

public arguments: -> Arguments uses Process = intrinsic

public environment name: Text -> Option<Text> uses Environment = intrinsic

# Runs one executable directly without a shell. The first item is the program
# and remaining items are literal argv entries.
public run argv: [Text; ~] -> Result<Int, Text> uses Process = intrinsic

public runToFile request: RunToFileRequest -> Result<Int, Text> uses Process, File = intrinsic

# Terminates the current process with the supplied status code. Compiler
# drivers use this after emitting a fatal diagnostic so no invalid artifact is
# mistaken for successful output.
public exit code: Int -> Unit uses Process = intrinsic

namespace sys.quic.keys

import sys.crypto.hkdf_sha256 as hkdf
import sys.crypto.tls13_hkdf as tls13

public struct InitialKeys {
    clientSecret: [UInt8; 32]
    serverSecret: [UInt8; 32]
    clientKey: [UInt8; 16]
    serverKey: [UInt8; 16]
    clientIv: [UInt8; 12]
    serverIv: [UInt8; 12]
    clientHeaderProtection: [UInt8; 16]
    serverHeaderProtection: [UInt8; 16]
}

public version1: -> UInt32 => 1
public version2: -> UInt32 => 1_798_521_807

v1Salt: -> [UInt8] => [56, 118, 44, 247, 245, 89, 52, 179, 77, 23,
    154, 230, 164, 200, 12, 173, 204, 187, 127, 10]

v2Salt: -> [UInt8] => [13, 237, 227, 222, 247, 0, 166, 219, 129, 147,
    129, 190, 110, 38, 157, 203, 249, 189, 46, 217]

public deriveInitial version: UInt32, destinationConnectionId: [UInt8] -> InitialKeys {
    version == version2() -> if { v2Salt() } else { v1Salt() } => salt
    [UInt8; ~] => empty
    hkdf.extract(salt, destinationConnectionId) => initialSecret
    initialSecret -> tls13.expandLabel32("client in", empty) => clientSecret
    initialSecret -> tls13.expandLabel32("server in", empty) => serverSecret
    version == version2() -> if { "quicv2 key" } else { "quic key" } => keyName
    version == version2() -> if { "quicv2 iv" } else { "quic iv" } => ivName
    version == version2() -> if { "quicv2 hp" } else { "quic hp" } => hpName
    clientSecret -> tls13.expandLabel16(keyName, empty) => clientKey
    serverSecret -> tls13.expandLabel16(keyName, empty) => serverKey
    clientSecret -> tls13.expandLabel12(ivName, empty) => clientIv
    serverSecret -> tls13.expandLabel12(ivName, empty) => serverIv
    clientSecret -> tls13.expandLabel16(hpName, empty) => clientHeaderProtection
    serverSecret -> tls13.expandLabel16(hpName, empty) => serverHeaderProtection
    InitialKeys {
        clientSecret: clientSecret
        serverSecret: serverSecret
        clientKey: clientKey
        serverKey: serverKey
        clientIv: clientIv
        serverIv: serverIv
        clientHeaderProtection: clientHeaderProtection
        serverHeaderProtection: serverHeaderProtection
    } => result
    result
}

namespace sys.runtime

public print value: Text -> Unit = intrinsic

public println value: Text -> Unit = intrinsic

public readInt prompt: Text -> Int = intrinsic

public seedRandom value: Int -> Unit = intrinsic

public randomBelow maxExclusive: Int -> Int = intrinsic

# Fills a newly allocated byte array from the operating system cryptographic
# random source. The runtime reports failure instead of falling back to the
# deterministic randomBelow generator.
public secureRandomBytes count: UIntSize -> Result<[UInt8; ~], sys.crypto.random.Error> uses Random = intrinsic

public openIntWriter path: Text -> Unit = intrinsic

public writeInt value: Int -> Unit = intrinsic

public closeIntWriter: -> Unit = intrinsic

public openIntReader path: Text -> Unit = intrinsic

public closestInt target: Int -> Int = intrinsic

public closeIntReader: -> Unit = intrinsic

public nowMillis: -> Long = intrinsic

public parallel<T, R> values: [T; ~] -> [R; ~] block item: T -> R = intrinsic

# Maps values concurrently and stops claiming new work after a callback returns
# Err. Already-started callbacks are joined before the deterministic earliest
# error or the ordered successful array is returned.
public tryParallel<T, R, E> values: [T; ~] -> Result<[R; ~], E> block item: T -> Result<R, E> = intrinsic

# Sets the bounded compute-pool size before its first use and returns the
# effective limit. Values below one become one; values above 64 become 64.
public limitParallelWorkers maxWorkers: Int -> Int = intrinsic

public parallelWorkers: -> Int = intrinsic

public parallelPeakWorkers: -> Int = intrinsic

public eprintln value: Text -> Unit = intrinsic

# Makes every preceding stdout byte observable before a program performs a
# blocking read. Native targets report a failed operating-system flush.
public flushStandardOutput: -> Unit uses Console = intrinsic

namespace sys.socket

# Numeric IP addresses keep name resolution outside the foundational socket
# contract. IPv4 and IPv6 text are accepted; host names belong to a later DNS
# layer with its own observable policy and errors.
public struct Endpoint {
    address: Text
    port: UInt16
}

public struct ListenOptions {
    endpoint: Endpoint
    backlog: Int
    reuseAddress: Bool
}

public struct DatagramBindOptions {
    endpoint: Endpoint
    reuseAddress: Bool
}

# TcpListener and TcpStream are affine native resources. Their private tokens
# cannot be constructed or copied by user code, and scope exit closes the
# underlying socket exactly once.
public struct TcpListener {
    token: UInt64
}

public struct TcpStream {
    token: UInt64
}

public struct UdpSocket {
    token: UInt64
}

# The source address is returned as owned UTF-8 bytes so receipt never hides a
# text allocation or DNS policy. It is the canonical numeric IPv4/IPv6 text
# emitted by the native platform.
public struct Datagram {
    sourceAddress: [UInt8; ~]
    sourcePort: UInt16
    bytes: [UInt8; ~]
}

public enum SocketErrorKind {
    InvalidAddress
    InvalidArgument
    AddressInUse
    ConnectionRefused
    ConnectionReset
    TimedOut
    Interrupted
    Unsupported
    Other
}

public struct SocketError {
    kind: SocketErrorKind
    code: Int32
}

# Creates a blocking TCP listener. backlog must be positive. Address parsing,
# socket creation, reuse-address setup, bind, and listen are one atomic
# operation: failure leaves no live native handle.
public listen options: ListenOptions -> Result<TcpListener, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Accept keeps the listener owner live and returns a new affine stream owner.
public accept listener: TcpListener -> Result<TcpStream, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Connect accepts only a numeric IPv4 or IPv6 address. DNS is intentionally not
# hidden inside this operation.
public connect endpoint: Endpoint -> Result<TcpStream, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Allocates one owned byte array with capacity maxBytes and publishes exactly
# the number of bytes received. An empty successful array means orderly peer
# shutdown. maxBytes must be positive.
public receive connection: TcpStream, maxBytes: UIntSize -> Result<[UInt8; ~], SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Sends at most bytes.len bytes and reports the exact count. A successful short
# send is observable so callers can implement an explicit retry policy.
public send connection: TcpStream, bytes: ref [UInt8; ~] -> Result<UIntSize, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Text is already UTF-8 storage, so this overload sends its bytes without
# allocation or transcoding and reports the exact count.
public sendText connection: TcpStream, text: Text -> Result<UIntSize, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Disables both directions while keeping deterministic owner close at scope
# exit. Calling shutdown more than once reports the native error.
public shutdown connection: TcpStream -> Result<Unit, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Creates a blocking UDP socket and binds it atomically. The socket is affine
# and closes exactly once at scope exit.
public bindDatagram options: DatagramBindOptions -> Result<UdpSocket, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Returns the port assigned to a bound UDP socket. This is especially useful
# after binding port 0, where the kernel selects an ephemeral port.
public localPort socket: UdpSocket -> Result<UInt16, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Sends one complete datagram. A successful result is the native byte count;
# callers must reject a short count if their protocol requires atomic delivery.
public sendTo socket: UdpSocket, endpoint: Endpoint, bytes: ref [UInt8; ~] -> Result<UIntSize, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic

# Receives one datagram up to maxBytes and returns its numeric source endpoint.
# maxBytes must be positive; larger datagrams follow the native truncation rule.
public receiveFrom socket: UdpSocket, maxBytes: UIntSize -> Result<Datagram, SocketError> uses Network = intrinsic
